rationale: All devices went offline simultaneously at ~7am after a router replacement, with the base station showing online=false, uplink=no_internet, and E-503 in logs. The base station LED was solid red. After reseating the Ethernet cable and power-cycling the router then base station, the LED turned solid blue and all cameras/sensors came back online — confirming a network uplink fault (L1), not a hardware failure.

repair_steps: Confirm base station LED is solid blue and all devices show online in app.
Advise customer to keep router and base station powered on and connected via Ethernet to a LAN port.
Document resolution: router replacement caused uplink loss; reseating cable and power-cycling router then base station restored connectivity.
Close ticket as resolved at frontline, no FAE escalation needed.
output.customer_reply: Great news! Your system is back online. The issue was caused by the new router's connection to the base station. After reseating the Ethernet cable and restarting the router and base station, everything is working normally. If you notice any devices offline again, please check the base station LED and contact us. Thank you for your patience!

args.question: What colour is the LED on the base station right now, and is the base station connected to the new router by an Ethernet cable or over Wi-Fi? (If Ethernet, which port is it plugged into on the router?)

args.action: Have the customer check the Ethernet cable on the base station: confirm it is plugged into a LAN port (not the WAN/Internet port) on the new router, and that the cable is firmly seated at both ends. Then power-cycle the router (unplug, wait 2 minutes, plug back in), wait for it to fully boot, then power-cycle the base station. Ask them to report the base station LED colour afterward.

results.text: The base station could not deliver events to the cloud. Frontline action: verify internet access, restart router and base station, set router DNS to automatic. If E-503 persists after these steps while the base station is online, escalate to FAE (cloud channel or certificate issue).
All devices offline, base station LED solid red. Router had been replaced the previous day and the Ethernet cable was in the wrong port. Resolved at frontline.

The base station connects to the home router by Ethernet (recommended) or 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. If all cameras and sensors show offline in the app at the same time, first check whether the base station itself is online. Power-cycle the router, wait 2 minutes, then power-cycle the base station. The base station requires outbound TCP 443 and 8883 to the cloud.
